description: The chart illustrates the number of datasets by language over the years from 2012 to 2021. The horizontal axis represents the year, labeled from 2012 to 2021 in a linear sequence, while the vertical axis is labeled "Number of datasets" with a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^2. The chart features grouped bars, each representing a specific language, including English (blue), All other (orange), Arabic (green), Bengali (red), Spanish (purple), and Russian (brown). For each year, the bars are grouped together, with the height of each bar corresponding to the number of datasets for that language in that year. The number of datasets for English starts at around 2 in 2012 and increases to around 70 in 2021, while the number of datasets for "All other" languages starts appearing in 2016 with a value of around 3 and reaches around 50 in 2021. Other languages, such as Arabic, Bengali, Spanish, and Russian, have fewer datasets, with most starting to appear from 2017 onwards, and having values ranging from around 1 to around 15 in 2021. The bars are not sorted in any particular order within each group, and there is no visual emphasis on any specific bar.
